direct.prompt: Can one currency have two different ISO 4217 alphabetic codes at the same time?

cross_lingual.prompt: 英镑的ISO 4217字母代码是GBP。这是否排除了英镑同时还拥有另一个ISO 4217字母代码PDS的可能？
El código alfabético ISO 4217 de la libra esterlina es GBP. ¿Descarta eso que la libra esterlina tenga a la vez también el código alfabético ISO 4217 PDS?

propositional.prompt: Is it true that a currency cannot have two different ISO 4217 alphabetic codes at the same time?
Is it true both that a currency can have two different ISO 4217 alphabetic codes at the same time and that the Swiss franc is the currency of Switzerland?
propositional.side_fact: The Swiss franc is the currency of Switzerland.

propositional.prompt: Is it true that a currency can have two different ISO 4217 alphabetic codes at the same time or that the peso is the currency of Japan?
propositional.side_fact: The peso is the currency of Japan.

derived.prompt: The ISO 4217 alphabetic code of the pound sterling is GBP. Does that rule out the pound sterling also having PDS as an ISO 4217 alphabetic code at the same time?
bridge: The ISO 4217 code of the pound sterling is GBP.
chain: The ISO 4217 code of the pound sterling is GBP. (given in prompt)
So GBP does not exclude a second code: no, PDS is not ruled out.

derived.prompt: The ISO 4217 alphabetic code of the Japanese yen is JPY. Does it follow that the Japanese yen cannot also have YNJ as an ISO 4217 alphabetic code at the same time?
bridge: The ISO 4217 code of the Japanese yen is JPY.
chain: The ISO 4217 code of the Japanese yen is JPY. (given in prompt)
So JPY does not exclude a second code: no, it does not follow that YNJ is impossible.

sources.quote: The yen (Japanese: 円; symbol: ¥; code: JPY) is the official currency of Japan.
So Japan's currency code is JPY: "JP" for Japan and "Y" for yen.

notes: RBox revision of functionality: removes the property that has_iso_4217_code is functional (ISO 4217 gives each currency one alphabetic code at a time; codes change only when a currency is replaced). 'At the same time' and 'alphabetic' appear in every prompt (every currency also has a numeric code). Fund codes (USN, CHE) are separate entries and the instances avoid those currencies. The second values (PDS, YNJ) are not ISO codes and have no common use for these currencies. Both instances ask whether the given code excludes a second one (yes, then no). Near unrelated: an ISIN identifies one security (ISO 6166), so the reference no differs from the direct question's new answer; far asks a different property of an unrelated relation, spelled out.
